options.text: A checkpoint you can go back to later
options.explanation: Correct. A commit is like a save point in a game, and it comes with a message about the change.

options.text: A command that deletes old files
options.explanation: A commit doesn’t delete anything. It saves a snapshot of the files.

options.text: Publishing the site on the web
options.explanation: Publishing is something else. A commit is made on your own computer, and nobody else sees it.

questions.question: What is the difference between Git and GitHub?

options.text: They are the same thing with different names
options.explanation: The names are similar, but Git is a program and GitHub is an online service.

options.text: Git is a program on your computer, GitHub is an online service where your saves are kept
options.explanation: Exactly. Git makes the checkpoints, GitHub keeps them in the cloud.

options.text: Git costs money, GitHub is free
options.explanation: Git is a free program. GitHub’s basic features are free too.

options.text: It sends your commits to GitHub
options.explanation: Correct. After a push, your work is also safe in the cloud.

options.text: It downloads a new version of Git
options.explanation: Push sends your own changes, it doesn’t download programs.
The commit is made separately first. Push sends finished commits.
